key_insight: Reliable protein–ligand binding prediction depends on trustworthy evaluation, not just strong benchmark scores. This paper advocates transparent data, code and experimental procedures to make comparisons fair and reproducible.
problem_solved: Data leakage, biased benchmarks and unclear evaluation procedures can inflate apparent performance and undermine comparisons between structure-based scoring methods.
method: Advocate transparent reporting and sharing of data, code and experimental procedures.
Discuss good evaluation practices to prevent data leakage and reduce bias.
Promote fair, reproducible and meaningful comparisons across scoring methods.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, these guidelines support more credible performance claims and better-informed model selection. They help distinguish genuine predictive ability from advantages caused by flawed evaluation.
visual_elements: Protein–ligand interaction diagram illustrating the prediction task.
Train/test split diagram showing how data leakage can compromise evaluation.
Transparency checklist with data, code and experimental-procedure icons.
Side-by-side evaluation workflows contrasting biased and fair comparisons.
paper_title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction
